newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan arrests group of 59 illegal Chinese.
newsitem.headline: Japan arrests group of 59 illegal Chinese.

text.p: Japanese maritime authorities arrested 59 Chinese trying to enter Japan on Wednesday after a 230 km (125 mile) high-seas chase.
The Chinese were on an 80-tonne fishing boat seized on Tuesday by Maritime Safety Agency (MSA) patrol boats in the Sea of Japan off Cape Daiozaki, 100 km (70 miles) south of Nagoya.
"When approached by the patrol boats the boat reversed its course and fled, but was stopped and seized after a 230 km chase," an MSA spokesman said.
He said the arrests added to growing worries about a sharp rise in the number of Chinese trying to sneak into Japan to take advantage of wages far higher than they could earn in their homeland.

"The arrest of these 59, coupled with the trend so far this year, suggests a significant rise in the number of Chinese nationals who are now becoming the vast majority of all illegal immigrants," the spokesman said.

"We"ve caught 168 Chinese out of 193 illegal immigrants so far this year, not including the latest group of 59 Chinese arrested. If it continues at this pace, this year will be the biggest on record for illegal immigrants," he added.
The spokesman said it was not yet clear whether Chinese brokers, known as "Snakeheads", were involved with the latest boat seized.
"We don"t know yet if there are any Chinese underworld connections running the immigration rings," he said.

Japan"s Foreign Ministry last week asked Beijing to crack down on smugglers running illegal immigrants into Japan as well as to step up China"s coastguard operations and inspections of ships leaving the country.
Police say "Snakeheads," mostly based in Taiwan and Hong Kong, charge as much as $30,000 for each illegal immigrant smuggled into Japan, and have close ties with Japan"s "Yakuza" gangsters.
